messages:
oliver: quick heads-up — ran a compact eval-matrix for L4 / T4 / A10G across us-west / eu-west / ap-southeast. focusing on two workloads: embeddings (batch=128) and small-chat (max_tokens=256, batch=1). sharing raw notes and a tiny summary.
priya: nice, did you include quantized runs? :eyes:
oliver: yup — fp16 baseline + q4_0 and q4_k. kernels tested: default runtime lib, fused-attn, and nvfuser where available. used the same model checkpoint for all runs (v1.2.0) to keep quality comparable.
mike: curious about region variance — network / infra differences?
oliver: region-level differences are small for pure GPU latency (we pinned to local colo), but infra differences affected cold-starts and provisioning time. numbers below are steady-state (no cold-start). benchbot: auto summary generated.
benchbot: SUMMARY (steady-state):
```
Embeddings qps (batch=128):
  us-west:  L4=1120 qps, T4=680 qps, A10G=970 qps
  eu-west:  L4=1080 qps, T4=660 qps, A10G=940 qps
  ap-south: L4=1020 qps, T4=620 qps, A10G=900 qps

Small-chat p95 latency (batch=1, 256 tokens):
  us-west:  L4=38ms, T4=72ms, A10G=44ms
  eu-west:  L4=42ms, T4=79ms, A10G=47ms
  ap-south: L4=48ms, T4=85ms, A10G=53ms

Cost per 1M tokens (approx):
  L4 ~ $28, T4 ~ $18, A10G ~ $22

Notes: q4_0 + fused-attn improved throughput by ~25% on L4 for embeddings with ~0.2% eval metric drift; on T4 q4_k gave larger gains but with slightly higher regression on small-chat outputs.
```
priya: interesting — L4 leads on latency + embeddings qps, but cost is highest. did you calculate cost-per-qps or cost-per-latency? we need the econ numbers for routing policy decisions.
oliver: quick derived numbers:
- embeddings cost-per-1k-queries (batchable): L4 = $0.025, T4 = $0.033, A10G = $0.023
- small-chat p95-adjusted-cost (favoring latency): normalized cost per p95-ms per 1M tokens: L4 = 0.74, T4 = 0.25, A10G = 0.50 (units are relative score; lower better because T4 is cheaper but slower)
(note: these are ballpark using our on-demand hourly rates + measured throughput)
mike: can you share where regressions showed up for q4? we need to know which evals to run automatically.
oliver: checked on our small-chat eval set (400 prompts):
- fp16 -> baseline BLEU-like quality = 0.81
- q4_0 on L4 -> 0.803 (delta -0.007)
- q4_k on T4 -> 0.78 (delta -0.03)
Qual diffs concentrated on rare tokenization-edge cases and math-like prompts.
yana: so TL;DR: L4 gives better latency and stable q4_0 gains, A10G is a balanced mid-cost option, T4 is cheapest but needs caution with quantization quality.
eva: any kernel-specific surprises?
oliver: yes — fused-attn gave noticeable wins on L4 (throughput +25% embeddings, p95 -8ms small-chat). nvfuser didn't improve much on A10G for this model; T4 benefited from some kernel patches (memory layout) in our runtime.
priya: for rollout, recommend: 
- hosted low-latency routes -> prefer L4 for interactive small-chat at SLO<=50ms.
- cost-sensitive batch embeddings -> A10G by default, fallback to L4 when latency requirement tighter.
- keep T4 as cold-surge capacity only if we gate q4_k quality tests.
mike: agree. add automated evals: run q4_k and q4_0 difference checks for every model push + failure threshold 1.5% metric delta.
oliver: noted. I'll add a tiny dashboard with these 3 numbers (latency p95, embeddings qps, quant-delta) per region + kernel. starting a PR to add gating in rollout pipeline.
priya: drop the raw CSV here pls so infra can reproduce.
oliver: attaching CSV snippet below:

benchbot: test-run ids: run-2026-03-19-1222 (us-west), run-2026-03-19-1234 (eu-west), run-2026-03-19-1248 (ap-southeast)
yana: thanks — if we see perf drift after kernel updates we should rebaseline across all regions. also flagging to platform: please ensure instance prewarming for L4 pools to avoid cold-start spikes.
oliver: yep will add prewarm policy proposal in the PR. anything else?
priya: let's schedule a 15m sync tomorrow to finalize rollout rubric. :calendar: 
mike: SGTM.
oliver: ended with action items in PR. thanks everyone. :rocket:
